test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 21 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: One Stop Centre scheme was launched on:
solution:
The correct answer is __**1st April 2015**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The One Stop Centre (OSC) scheme was launched on **1st April 2015** by the Government of India.
 
• The scheme aims to provide **integrated support and assistance to women affected by violence**, in both private and public spaces under one roof.
 
• OSC is a sub-scheme of the **National Mission for Empowerment of Women** (NMEW) and also known as **Sakhi**.
 
• The centres offer a range of services including medical aid, police assistance, legal aid/counselling, psycho-social counselling, and temporary shelter to women.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Mission for Empowerment of Women (NMEW)**

 
 
• Launched by the Government of India in 2010, NMEW aims at strengthening the overall processes that promote all-round development of women.
 
• The mission focuses on inter-sectoral issues affecting women, particularly those related to health, education, and economic empowerment.
 
• NMEW works towards creating an enabling environment for women through convergence of schemes/programs of different ministries/departments.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS)**
 
 
• ICPS is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at building a protective environment for children in difficult circumstances, as well as other vulnerable children, through government-civil society partnership.
 
• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development and focuses on the needs and rights of children, ensuring their safety and protection.
 
• ICPS provides for care, support, and rehabilitation services to children in need, including those who are victims of abuse, exploitation, and neglect.
 
 
 
• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)**
 
 
• Launched on 22nd January 2015 by the Government of India, BBBP aims to address the declining child sex ratio (CSR) and related issues of women empowerment over a life-cycle continuum.
 
• The scheme is a tri-ministerial effort of the Ministries of Women and Child Development, Health & Family Welfare, and Human Resource Development.
 
• BBBP focuses on changing the mindset towards the girl child and ensuring education and participation of girls in all aspects of life.
